root_idea.summary: The root centers on bringing a built thing down from its standing state: demolishing, dismantling, or collapsing a structure.
root_idea.development: The core image extends to things reduced to ruin or forfeited, with related nominal uses for a worn-out garment, wasted blood, and earth excavated from a pit or well. These extensions are not all Quranic.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form هَدَّمَ rather than the inflected passive Quran occurrence هُدِّمَتْ.

senses.definition: To demolish or destroy a building or other structure; in the attested passive construction, to be demolished.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran occurrence is a passive perfect Form II verb with a structure as the affected object. Form II may convey intensified or thorough demolition in this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into ruin or collapse by degrees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive construction used of structures that progressively fall apart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collapse, fall to pieces, or become a ruin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive construction; it can describe a structure falling from its place without being actively pulled to pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth dug out from a pit or well.
Blood regarded as wasted or left unavenged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use in the expression دم هَدْمٌ.
The noun is used in this specialized nominal sense, with the plural أهدام reported in the lexical evidence.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Demolition and destruction of a structure are covered by the Quranic sense.
Progressive collapse is represented as a distinct intransitive construction.
Intransitive collapse and becoming a ruin are represented.
The spontaneous falling of a wall from its place is covered by the intransitive collapse meaning.
Pointer-only cross-reference to another root entry.
The lexical meaning of earth excavated from a pit or well is represented.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is a passive Form II form; the Form VI and Form VII entries are separate Classical intransitive constructions.
